author: Maya (Platform)
text: For the billing ledger, PostgreSQL gives us transactions, foreign keys, and predictable relational queries. MongoDB would make the evolving event payload easy, but the ledger invariants matter more.

author: Omar (Backend)
text: Agreed on PostgreSQL. We can keep flexible provider payloads in JSONB while retaining transactional updates for invoices and payments. Decision: PostgreSQL for the billing service.

author: Lina (SRE)
text: The pricing endpoint repeatedly recomputes the same plan catalog and is our largest read-latency spike. A short Redis cache with a 60-second TTL should reduce duplicate database reads without making plan changes stale for long.

author: Omar (Backend)
text: Let's introduce Redis only for the plan catalog lookup, use key pricing:plans:v1, and fall back to PostgreSQL when Redis is unavailable. We are not using Redis as the source of truth.

author: Noor (API)
text: Partner retries are creating request bursts. Apply a per-API-key token bucket at 120 requests per minute and return Retry-After with HTTP 429 so clients can back off predictably.

author: Lina (SRE)
text: The rate limit should fail open if the limiter store is briefly unavailable; availability is preferable to rejecting every partner request during a cache incident.

author: Ari (Security)
text: Structured logs must omit session_id, access_token, and email. Keep request_id for debugging and store only the allowlisted fields needed for incident response.

author: Maya (Platform)
text: Approved: redact sensitive fields before serialization, not in the log collector. That prevents secrets from entering local buffers or downstream log storage.
